case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to St. Joseph first.** I'd expect pier fishing there to be slow to below average this week, about a **1** on your scale.
- **South Haven is about a 1 as well**, but its pier reports are less consistent.
- **Grand Haven and Muskegon are about a 0 to 1.** Grand Haven's latest pier report was slow, and Muskegon has had no pier report since Sept 18.
- **Bring spoons and spinners, with glow spoons for early morning and low light.** The St. Joseph pier did well on spinners and spoons, and glow spoons worked at several piers when the light was low.
- **Don't count on a good day from the pier.** Plan a backup such as the St. Joseph River, which reported good salmon catches on Sept 11.

## Why

- **St. Joseph has the best pier outlook:** its latest pier report (Oct 2) was "on the slow side" but still had a few fish, and it is the only pier in the recent reports rated good (Sept 11).
- **Grand Haven ranks lowest:** its last three pier reports (Sept 18, Sept 25, Oct 2) were all rated slow.
- **I'd expect slow to fair pier fishing overall:** past early-October weeks with surface water near 64 to 67 F mostly had slow piers.

## Evidence

**Recent reports (newest is Oct 2, six days old):**
- St. Joseph, Oct 2: pier "on the slow side for salmon, however there were a few fish caught" (quality 1). Boats did better "in the near pier areas" on spoons (quality 2).
- South Haven, Oct 2: "The piers were very inconsistent for salmon" (quality 1).
- Grand Haven, Oct 2: "Pier anglers casting spoons for mature salmon found the action to be slow" (quality 0). Sept 25 and Sept 18 were also slow (quality 0).
- Muskegon: the Sept 18 pier report was slow ("unsuccessful," quality 0). Sept 11 was quality 1, with a few fish on glow spoons. No pier report since.
- St. Joseph, Sept 11: "good numbers of salmon" from the pier, mostly on spinners and spoons (quality 3). This is the only good pier report in the four weeks, and it came during a possible upwelling.
- Pier depths are not given in these reports.

**Past seasons (general history, matched on water temperature near 65 F):**
- Oct 2023 and Oct 2022 piers at these ports were mostly slow. Oct 4, 2023 Grand Haven: "No salmon were reported to be caught from the piers." Oct 4, 2023 South Haven: an occasional coho or Chinook (quality 1).
- Sept 20, 2023 Grand Haven: a few salmon on early-morning glow spoons (quality 1).

**Conditions now (weekly summary, not live):**
- Buoy surface water for the week before Oct 8: St. Joseph averaged 67 F (-1 F over the week). South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon averaged 64 F (+5 F over the week).
- The +5 F rise at three ports suggests warming, not upwelling. I'd expect a sharp drop, which would be the cue to head to the piers, to be the thing that would change this.
- No modeled pierhead water or wind forecast was returned, so I can't check for upwelling or wind at the piers.

## Caveats

- **The newest report is six days old** (Oct 2). Conditions can change quickly this time of year.
- **The water data is a summary of the week before Oct 8, not live readings.** The buoy readings are measured offshore. Pierhead temperatures and the wind forecast were not available.
- **Muskegon and South Haven have thin pier data.** Muskegon's last pier report was Sept 18, and South Haven's ratings have been inconsistent.
- **General guidance:** Michigan Sea Grant says a sharp drop in surface temperature (upwelling) brings salmon toward piers, and NY DEC says Chinook prefer 52 to 58 F. I haven't checked either against this week's data.

## Sources

- Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph, Oct 2 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3b980f9
- Sept 25 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3b7fd3a
- Sept 18 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3b67fce
- Sept 11 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3b5093d
- Oct 4, 2023 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/37424d6
- Sept 20, 2023 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3717a83
